collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE II: THE LAND, MEMORY AND NEW TRADITIONS (LCB-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
Isola's ceremonies for the land and sea, its ways of remembering and mourning, and the new traditions its people make, question and change: rain songs, reef promises, memory gardens, funerals, forgotten melodies and festivals nobody planned.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A newcomer offers to teach the children words from their homeland: hold lessons, or just let it happen at play.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) came to Isola last year, and still speaks the language of (subject.his/her) homeland when (subject.he/she) is tired or happy. (friend) has asked (subject.him/her) to teach (friend.him/her) some words. Now half the children want to learn. (subject) is touched, and a little nervous. How should (subject.he/she) teach them?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) holds lessons every evening under the old fig. The children learn colors, animals, and a very rude word for crab, which they use constantly. Before long the adults are asking for lessons too.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) just talks to the children in (subject.his/her) language while they play, and lets them pick it up. Within a month, (friend) can count to twenty and sing a whole song. (subject) hears it from across the village one evening and has to sit down for a moment.
